```{r}
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)  # For p-values
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
```

```{r}
size_data <- read.csv("D:/First Year Resit Exam/Project Multivariate and Hierarchical Data/Project/G10.size.data.csv")
```


```{r}
size_data$climate <- as.factor(size_data$climate)
size_data$species <- as.factor(size_data$species)
size_data$tree_id <- as.factor(size_data$tree_id)
size_data$time <- as.numeric(size_data$time) 
```


```{r}
model <- lmer(size ~ 0 + climate:time + species:time + climate:species:time + (0 + time | pear_id), data = size_data, 
              REML = FALSE)

# Summarize the model
summary(model)
```

```{r}
model2 <- lmer(size ~ 0 + time : climate + species : time + (0 + time | pear_id), data = size_data, REML = FALSE)
  
# Summarize the model
summary(model2)
confint(model2)
```
```{r}
vc <- VarCorr(model2)
vc

# EB (BLUP) random effects
re <- ranef(model2, condVar = TRUE)$pear_id  # columns: (Intercept), time
re$pear_id <- rownames(re)

# Summaries for the random slope
summ <- re %>% summarize(
  mean = mean(time), sd = sd(time),
  p05 = quantile(time, 0.05), p50 = median(time),
  p95 = quantile(time, 0.95), min = min(time), max = max(time)
)
summ

# Caterpillar plot (random slopes with intervals)
library(ggplot2)
re_ord <- re %>% arrange(time) %>% mutate(rank = row_number())
ggplot(re_ord, aes(rank, time)) + geom_point() +
  labs(x = "Pear (ordered)", y = "EB random slope (deviation)")
```



```{r}
library(lme4)

# Apply quadratic transformation to time
size_data$quad_time <- poly(size_data$time, 2)

# Fit the mixed model with quadratic time and interactions
model_quad <- lmer(size ~ quad_time : climate + species : quad_time + (1 + quad_time | pear_id), 
                   data = size_data, REML = FALSE)

# Summarize results
summary(model_quad)



```

```{r}
size_data$log_size <- log(size_data$size + 1)  # Ensure no log(0) errors
model_exp <- lmer(log_size ~ time : climate + species : time + (1 + time | pear_id), 
                  data = size_data, REML = FALSE)
summary(model_exp)
```

```{r}
# Aggregate mean and CI for plot
plot_data <- size_data %>%
  group_by(time, climate, species) %>%
  summarise(mean_size = mean(size), .groups = "drop")

# Plot with centered title
ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = time, y = mean_size, color = climate, linetype = species)) +
  geom_line(size = 1.1) +
  labs(title = "Pear Growth Over Time by Climate and Species",
       x = "Week",
       y = "Average Size (cm)",
       color = "Climate",
       linetype = "Species") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))


```



```{r}
#+=========================================================================
# 1. Load emmeans and fit your model (if not already done)
library(emmeans)
# assume your model is named `growth_model_lmer`

# 2. Extract the estimated slopes ("trends") for time by species×climate
trends <- emtrends(
  model2,
  ~ species * climate,  # this creates one estimate per species:climate
  var = "time",  pbkrtest.limit = 5000
)

# 3. Check the order of the levels, so you know how the contrast vectors map
summary(trends)
# It will list the 8 combinations in this order by default:
#   1 Conference:Scenario1
#   2 Doyenne:Scenario1
#   3 Conference:Scenario2
#   4 Doyenne:Scenario2
#   5 Conference:Scenario3
#   6 Doyenne:Scenario3
#   7 Conference:Scenario4
#   8 

# 4. Define your contrasts exactly as in SAS:
my_contrasts <- list(
  "C_1 vs C_2" = c( 1,  0, -1,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0),
  "C_1 vs C_3" = c( 1,  0,  0,  0, -1,  0,  0,  0),
  "C_1 vs C_4" = c( 1,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0, -1,  0),
  "D_1 vs D_2" = c( 0,  1,  0, -1,  0,  0,  0,  0),
  "D_1 vs D_3" = c( 0,  1,  0,  0,  0, -1,  0,  0),
  "D_1 vs D_4" = c( 0,  1,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0, -1),
  "C_1 vs D_1" = c( 1, -1,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0,  0)
)

# 5. Apply the contrasts with a Bonferroni correction (or none, as you wish)
contrast_results <- contrast(trends, method = my_contrasts, adjust = "bonferroni")

# 6. Summarize
summary(contrast_results)
confint(contrast_results)

```

# Plot observed vs fitted

```{r}

# Q-Q plot
qqnorm(resid(model2))
qqline(resid(model2), col = "red")

```
